q-119896.name: Question 1
q-119896.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251898/assets/212a339585b98f156d68f2e4260c0acbb474c51782b6d72acf0b89fd5c1fe69e.png)

Given the vectors $a$ and $b$ shown above, which of the following could be the linear combination $2a-2b?$
q-119896.worked_solution:
First, recall that

$$
2a-2b=2a+(-2b).
$$

- The vector $2a$ has the same direction as $a$ but twice the magnitude.

- The vector $-2b$ has the direction that is opposite to $b$ but twice the magnitude.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251898/assets/c1cc845ddfe16f12169625e5f8404d3d92558b885ffde8c3ab02cdb2c096f699.png)

Now, we can draw $-2b$ starting from the head of $2a.$ The resultant 

$$
2a-2b
$$

goes from the tail of $2a$ to the head of $-2b.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251898/assets/5d22db7e37ff1c5b55f1ec595da919f987a6c1fea4247cf5a075f27c198ba545.png)

q-277079.name: Question 4
q-277079.problem:
Suppose we are given two vectors $a$ and $b$ where $a∦b.$ Find $\lambda $ and $\mu ,$ if 

$$
a-2b=(3\lambda -\mu )a-(\lambda -4\mu )b.
$$

$\lambda =$
{{field-1}}$,\,\mu =$
{{field-2}}
q-277079.worked_solution:
Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. So, the coefficients of $a$ must be equal, and the coefficients of $b$ must be equal.

Equating the coefficients, we get:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3\lambda -\mu =1 \\ \lambda -4\mu =2\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain:

$$
\mu =3\lambda -1
$$

Substituting back into the second equation, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda -4\mu  & =2 \\ \lambda -4(3\lambda -1) & =2 \\ \lambda -12\lambda +4 & =2 \\ -11\lambda  & =-2 \\ \lambda  & =\frac{2}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =3\lambda -1 \\  & =3\cdot \frac{2}{11}-1 \\  & =-\frac{5}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-11381.name: Question 5
q-11381.problem:
Suppose we are given two vectors $a$ and $b$ where $a∦b.$ Find $s$ and $t,$ if 

$$
5a+4b=(2s+t)a+(s-t)b.
$$
q-11381.worked_solution:
Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. So, the coefficients of $a$ must be equal, and the coefficients of $b$ must be equal.

Equating the coefficients, we get:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2s+t=5 \\ s-t=4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}3s & =9 \\ s & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting back into the first equation, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}2s+t & =5 \\ 2(3)+t & =5 \\ 6+t & =5 \\ t & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that $s=3$ and $t=-1.$
